extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, institutional research administrators, grant applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and guidance relevant to preparing and managing grant applications and awards. Items highlight expectations (e.g., data sharing, reproducibility), program changes, and review policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models (including New Approach Methodologies, NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease; investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize human relevance and translational potential when choosing models. New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) are encouraged as long as they are scientifically sound and appropriately matched to the research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand PF5 Collaborative International Research Project application structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 6-minute video overview explains key features, application format, and how Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review the PF5 overview to learn required application format details and be prepared for the possibility that an application could be split into linked awards post-review (before JIT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans for applicable proposals, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified by NIH for pilot submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The reliability of biomedical research is foundational; NIH's Gold Standard Science plan encourages a culture valuing replication and reproducibility and the agency launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize such efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should incorporate replication and reproducibility considerations into study design, methods, and proposed activities where relevant. Expect NIH to highlight replication/reproducibility as an emphasized topic and to offer initiatives and incentives supporting these practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' scoring after review modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications after a lapse in appropriations, applications in the middle third of a study section were designated 'competitive but not discussed' when strong applications fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who receive a 'competitive but not discussed' designation should understand this can reflect peer review cutoffs rather than a definitive judgment of merit; policies on triage and discussion thresholds (e.g., the 33% cutoff) affect which applications are discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of centralized peer review consolidation effects
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH centralized all peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) in March 2025; initial effects include expected impacts on efficiency, competition, and transparency in the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators and institutions should monitor how centralization affects review timelines, study section assignments, and competitiveness; consult NIH notices and Nexus updates for operational changes stemming from the consolidation.
